title: Adaptive B-Tree Rebalancing
description: Monitors page split and merge rates and rebalances hot B-tree branches during low-traffic windows instead of on the write path. By deferring structural work to idle periods, foreground writes never pay rebalance latency. The controller uses split-rate telemetry to decide which subtrees need attention.
key_mechanisms: Track page split/merge rates per subtree
Schedule rebalances in low-traffic windows
Verify depth invariants after each rebalance

demo.title: Demo — Adaptive B-Tree Rebalancing

title: Learned Index Auto-Tuning
description: Replaces static B-tree fanout with learned models such as recursive model indexes and retrains when key-distribution drift exceeds a threshold. When the data is smooth, lookups become near-O(1); the tuner watches prediction error and falls back to a B-tree when drift gets bad. It is the frontier of self-tuning storage.
key_mechanisms: Train recursive models over the key space
Monitor prediction error as a drift signal
Fall back to B-tree when error exceeds bounds

demo.title: Demo — Learned Index Auto-Tuning

title: Hot-Key Partition Splitting
description: Detects skewed partitions by request heat and splits them without downtime, migrating the hottest key ranges first. Heat is measured per key range over sliding windows, and the splitter moves just enough ranges to bring the hottest node under 120 percent of mean load. Clients see no interruption because routing updates atomically.
key_mechanisms: Measure per-range request heat in sliding windows
Split the hottest ranges first
Update routing tables atomically

demo.title: Demo — Hot-Key Partition Splitting

title: Query-Driven Column Reordering
description: Reorders columns in wide tables so the most-filtered columns sit first for better zone-map pruning. The analyzer mines the query log for predicate frequency, then rewrites the table layout so scans skip the most data. It is especially effective on event tables with dozens of rarely-filtered columns.
key_mechanisms: Mine predicate frequency from the query log
Place high-selectivity columns first
Rewrite layout during maintenance windows

demo.title: Demo — Query-Driven Column Reordering

title: Bitmap vs B-Tree Auto-Switching
description: Converts low-cardinality indexes between bitmap and B-tree forms based on observed selectivity and update rates. Bitmaps win for read-heavy low-cardinality predicates; B-trees win when updates are frequent. The switcher measures both and converts the index form online when the crossover point moves.
key_mechanisms: Track selectivity and update rate per index
Compute the bitmap/B-tree crossover point
Convert the index form online

demo.title: Demo — Bitmap vs B-Tree Auto-Switching

title: Online Index Defragmentation
description: Rebuilds fragmented indexes incrementally using a spare I/O budget, pausing whenever foreground latency rises. Fragmentation is measured as the gap ratio between logically adjacent pages, and the defragmenter compacts the worst segments first. It keeps long-lived tables fast without maintenance downtime.
key_mechanisms: Measure page-gap fragmentation ratios
Compact worst segments within an I/O budget
Pause when foreground latency rises

demo.title: Demo — Online Index Defragmentation

title: Composite Index Key Reordering
description: Reorders composite key columns to match the most common predicate prefix seen in the slow-query log. A composite index on (a, b, c) only helps queries filtering on a, or a and b — so the order must follow real query shapes. The rewriter proposes new orders and validates them against captured plans.
key_mechanisms: Extract predicate prefixes from the query log
Rank candidate column orders by coverage
Validate with EXPLAIN before rebuilding

demo.title: Demo — Composite Index Key Reordering

title: Covering Index Auto-Creation
description: Proposes and builds covering indexes for repeated index-only scan opportunities, then drops them if unused for 30 days. The advisor watches for queries that repeatedly fetch the same few columns and materializes an index containing exactly those columns. Automatic expiry prevents index bloat.
key_mechanisms: Detect repeated index-only scan opportunities
Build covering indexes with exact column sets
Drop indexes unused for 30 days

demo.title: Demo — Covering Index Auto-Creation

title: Stale Index Pruning
description: Drops indexes with zero reads over a full workload cycle, reclaiming the write amplification they cost on every insert and update. Usage stats are collected per index, and anything unread through a complete business cycle is a candidate for removal. It is the simplest self-tuning win most databases never do.
key_mechanisms: Collect per-index read counters
Flag indexes unread for a full cycle
Drop after a grace period with rollback

demo.title: Demo — Stale Index Pruning

title: LSM Compaction Scheduling
description: Shapes LSM-tree compaction strategy to the workload: leveled for read-heavy, tiered for write bursts, switching automatically as the mix changes. Leveled compaction minimizes read amplification at the cost of write amplification; the scheduler picks the cheaper side from live metrics. Getting this wrong is the top LSM performance pitfall.
key_mechanisms: Measure read vs write amplification live
Switch leveled/tiered strategy at crossover
Throttle compaction within write budgets

demo.title: Demo — LSM Compaction Scheduling

title: Hash Partition Rehashing
description: Grows consistent-hash ring virtual nodes when a node exceeds 120 percent of mean load, rebalancing with minimal key movement. Virtual nodes let the system shift fine-grained slices of the key space instead of whole partitions. Rehashing is staged so clients never observe partial routing.
key_mechanisms: Monitor per-node load vs the ring mean
Add virtual nodes to overloaded members
Stage routing updates to avoid partial views

demo.title: Demo — Hash Partition Rehashing

title: Statistics-Driven Plan Invalidation
description: Invalidates cached query plans when table statistics shift beyond confidence bounds, forcing the optimizer to re-plan. Stale plans are a classic cause of sudden slowdowns after bulk loads; the invalidator compares new histograms against the ones the plan was built with. Only affected plans are dropped, not the whole cache.
key_mechanisms: Version histograms per table
Compare plan-time stats to current stats
Invalidate only plans outside confidence bounds

demo.title: Demo — Statistics-Driven Plan Invalidation

title: Spatial Index Retiling
description: Retiles R-tree and quadtree cells when point density changes, keeping nearest-neighbor queries logarithmic. As data clusters move — new stores opening, old ones closing — static tiles become lopsided and queries slow down. The retiler rebuilds the spatial partition from current density maps.
key_mechanisms: Build density maps from current data
Repartition tiles to balance point counts
Rebuild the spatial index online

demo.title: Demo — Spatial Index Retiling

title: Inverted Index Term Pruning
description: Drops posting lists for terms that never appear in queries, shrinking the index and speeding up merges. Query logs reveal a long tail of indexed terms nobody searches; pruning them cuts merge I/O with zero user impact. Pruned terms can be re-added if query patterns change.
key_mechanisms: Join the term dictionary against query logs
Drop posting lists for never-queried terms
Re-add terms if query patterns shift

demo.title: Demo — Inverted Index Term Pruning

title: Materialized View Reselection
description: Recomputes which views to materialize from recent query fingerprints, replacing low-hit views with high-value ones. The selector scores candidate views by estimated query-time savings minus refresh cost, then swaps the set during low-traffic windows. It turns materialized views from a DBA art into a control loop.
key_mechanisms: Fingerprint recent queries for view candidates
Score candidates by savings minus refresh cost
Swap the materialized set in low-traffic windows
